Expressway: An expressway with several lanes and roadside metal guardrails or barriers.
Ordinary highway: An ordinary highway with natural scenery along the roadside.
Mountain road: A winding mountain road, possibly with a mountain slope or cliff on one side.
Urban expressway: An elevated urban road or urban expressway with a wide carriageway, a central divider, full access control, no traffic lights, and possibly noise barriers along the sides.
Ordinary urban road: An urban street lined with buildings, street trees, streetlights, shops, and sidewalks.
Residential access road: A forward-facing driving image inside a residential area, with a relatively narrow road, residential buildings and parked vehicles along the sides, and possibly passing pedestrians.
Road section: A forward-facing driving image on a straight road section.
Ramp: A forward-facing driving image on a road ramp that may curve rather than run straight.
Conventional intersection: A forward-facing driving image at a four-way or three-way intersection.
Roundabout: A forward-facing driving image at a roundabout or circular intersection.
Bridge: A forward-facing driving image on a bridge, possibly with guardrails or a river alongside.
Tunnel: A forward-facing driving image inside a tunnel.
Railway level crossing: A forward-facing driving image near a railway level crossing, possibly showing tracks and barriers.
On-street parking space: Rectangular parking space markings along the roadside, possibly occupied by vehicles.
Motor vehicle lane: A forward-facing driving image on a road with designated lane types, including a lane for motor vehicles.
Acceleration lane: An image taken in an expressway acceleration lane, with a merging lane on the right for vehicles to accelerate onto the main carriageway.
Deceleration lane: An image taken in an expressway deceleration lane, with an exit lane on the right for vehicles to slow down and leave the main carriageway.
Sidewalk: A road with designated lane types and a sidewalk paved with bricks or concrete along the roadside for pedestrians.
Non-motorized vehicle lane: A roadside non-motorized vehicle lane reserved for bicycles or electric bicycles, possibly separated by barriers.
No separation of lane types: A forward-facing driving image on a mixed-use road without clearly separated motor vehicle lanes, non-motorized vehicle lanes, or sidewalks.
Bus-only lane: A forward-facing driving image showing a bus-only lane identified by yellow dashed lines or bus-lane text markings.
Emergency lane: A forward-facing driving image showing an emergency lane at the far right of an expressway or urban expressway, usually separated by a solid line.
No exclusive lane designation: A forward-facing driving image showing an ordinary motor vehicle lane without special exclusive-use markings.
Normal-width lane: A forward-facing driving image on a road with normal-width lanes and ample space for vehicles.
Narrow lane: A forward-facing driving image on a road with narrow lanes and limited space for vehicles.
Sharp bend: A sharply bending road whose direction changes abruptly.
Normal road alignment: A normal road with a gentle, straight alignment.
Steep uphill grade: The road ahead rises sharply uphill, obstructing the view.
Steep downhill grade: The road ahead descends sharply downhill.
One lane per direction: There is only one lane in the vehicle's direction of travel, and the road is relatively narrow.
Two lanes per direction: There are two parallel lanes in the vehicle's direction of travel.
More than two lanes per direction: There are at least three parallel lanes in the vehicle's direction of travel, and the road is relatively wide.
More than three lanes per direction: There are at least four parallel lanes in the vehicle's direction of travel, and the road is very wide.
Fewer lanes ahead: The road narrows ahead, with the number of lanes decreasing or lanes merging.
More lanes ahead: The road widens ahead, with an increasing number of lanes.
Unchanged lane count ahead: The number of lanes remains unchanged ahead.
Normal road surface: A forward-facing driving image on a road with a normal, dry, and even surface.
Snow- or ice-covered road surface: A forward-facing driving image on a road covered with snow or ice, with an apparently slippery surface.
Muddy road surface: A forward-facing driving image on a road covered with mud or wet soil, with an apparently uneven surface.
Flooded road: A forward-facing driving image on a road with substantial standing water or a flooded surface.
One-way traffic: A one-way road where all vehicles travel in the same direction, without a centerline or median divider in the middle.
Two-way traffic: A two-way road, possibly separated by a centerline or median divider.
Main road: A forward-facing driving image taken on a main road carrying the primary flow of traffic.
Service road: A forward-facing driving image taken on a service road alongside a main road, serving local access and traffic.
Bus stop within 30 m: A bus stop platform or bus stop sign is visible nearby along the roadside.
Emergency medical station within 30 m: A sign for a hospital emergency center or emergency medical station is visible nearby along the roadside.
Gas station within 30 m: A gas station canopy, fuel pumps, or a gas station sign is visible nearby along the roadside.
Fire hydrant within 30 m: A fire hydrant is visible nearby along the roadside.
Fire station within 30 m: A fire station or fire brigade building is visible nearby along the roadside.
Intersection within 50 m: A road intersection is immediately ahead.
Railway level crossing within 50 m: A railway level crossing is immediately ahead, with warning signs or barriers.
Sharp bend within 50 m: The road ahead bends sharply to the left or right.
Road less than 4 m wide within 50 m: The road ahead suddenly becomes unusually narrow.
Bridge within 50 m: A bridge is ahead and is about to be entered, possibly with guardrails or a river along its sides.
Steep grade within 50 m: A steep grade lies ahead, with a sharp uphill slope in the road.
Tunnel within 50 m: A tunnel entrance is ahead, and the vehicle is about to enter it.
White Solid line: A continuous, unbroken White Solid line painted on the road surface.
White dashed line: A broken white dashed line painted on the road surface.
Yellow solid line: A continuous, unbroken yellow solid line painted on the road surface.
Yellow dashed line: A broken yellow dashed line painted on the road surface.
Double solid white lines: Two adjacent, parallel, continuous White Solid lines painted on the road surface.
Double dashed white lines: Two adjacent, parallel white dashed lines painted on the road surface.
Double solid yellow lines: Two adjacent, parallel, continuous yellow solid lines painted on the road surface.
Double dashed yellow lines: Two adjacent, parallel yellow dashed lines painted on the road surface.
White solid-and-dashed lines: Two adjacent, parallel lines painted on the road surface: one white dashed line and one continuous White Solid line.
Yellow solid-and-dashed lines: Two adjacent, parallel lines painted on the road surface: one yellow dashed line and one continuous yellow solid line.
Pedestrian crossing markings: A set of broad white zebra stripes painted on the road surface to mark a pedestrian crossing.
Stop line: A thick white transverse line before an intersection indicating where vehicles should stop.
Box junction marking: A yellow crosshatched marking on the road surface indicating an area where stopping is prohibited.
Directional arrow: A white directional arrow painted on the road surface indicating straight-ahead travel, a turn, or a U-turn.
channelizing line: A channelizing line formed by white diagonal hatching or a V-shaped area on the road surface, indicating traffic separation.
Lane divider marking: White dashed or solid lines painted on the road surface to separate different lanes.
Bus-only lane marking: Yellow or white road markings bearing the words 'BUS ONLY'.
Speed limit pavement marking: A speed limit number, such as 60, painted directly on the road surface.
No speed limit pavement marking present: A forward-facing driving image with no speed limit numbers painted on the visible road surface.
No left turn prohibition marking present: A forward-facing driving image with no pavement marking prohibiting left turns visible.
No U-turn prohibition marking present: A forward-facing driving image with no pavement marking prohibiting U-turns visible.
No road markings: No road markings are painted on the visible part of the road surface.
Red traffic light: A forward-facing driving image showing a traffic signal displaying a red stop light.
Green traffic light: A forward-facing driving image showing a traffic signal displaying a green proceed light.
Yellow traffic light: A forward-facing driving image showing a traffic signal displaying a yellow warning light.
No traffic signals: A forward-facing driving image with no traffic signals or with traffic signals that are not operating.
No U-turn sign: A circular no U-turn sign with a red border, a white background, and a black U-turn arrow crossed by a red diagonal slash.
No left turn sign: A circular no left turn sign with a red border, a white background, and a black left-turn arrow crossed by a red diagonal slash.
No stopping sign: A circular no stopping sign with a red border, a blue background, and a red cross in the center.
No honking sign: A circular no honking sign with a red border, a white background, and a horn symbol crossed by a red diagonal slash.
Speed limit sign: A speed limit sign: a circular traffic sign with a red border, a white background, and a black speed limit number in the center.
Warning sign: A yellow triangular traffic sign with a black border and a black symbol on a yellow background.
No U-turn prohibition sign present: A forward-facing driving image with no sign prohibiting U-turns visible.
No left turn prohibition sign present: A forward-facing driving image with no sign prohibiting left turns visible.
No speed limit sign present: A forward-facing driving image with no speed limit sign visible.
No traffic signs: No traffic signs are visible in the field of view.
Road centerline: Opposing traffic directions are separated only by a painted road centerline, dashed or solid, without a physical barrier.
Median divider: Opposing traffic directions are physically separated by a median divider consisting of a planted strip, metal guardrail, or concrete barriers.
No central road separation: There are no separation facilities or road centerline in the middle of the road, leaving an uninterrupted road surface.
Ambulance: An ambulance with a red cross symbol on its body.
Police vehicle: A police vehicle with police insignia and emergency lights.
Fire engine: A red fire engine equipped with an aerial ladder or water cannon.
Roadworks: A forward-facing driving image showing roadworks with construction barriers, traffic cones, or construction signs on the road.
Traffic accident: A forward-facing driving image showing a vehicle collision or traffic accident, possibly with damaged vehicles stopped on the road.
Obstacles on the road: A forward-facing driving image showing stones, cargo, or other obstacles scattered on the road and obstructing traffic.
Vehicle breakdown: A forward-facing driving image showing an apparently broken-down vehicle stopped at the roadside or on the road with hazard lights on and a warning triangle behind it.
Traffic police directing traffic: A forward-facing driving image showing a traffic police officer in a uniform or reflective vest directing traffic with hand signals on the road.
No traffic police directing traffic: A forward-facing driving image without traffic police directing traffic.
Traffic management personnel directing t: A forward-facing driving image showing a traffic management worker in a reflective vest directing traffic with hand signals.
Foggy weather: Foggy weather with dense fog, low visibility, and blurred distant scenery.
Rainy weather: Rainy weather with falling rain, raindrops on the windshield, and a wet, slippery, reflective road surface.
Snowy weather: Snowy weather with falling snow and snow covering the road or surrounding area.
Dusty weather: Dusty weather with a dust storm.
Daytime: A forward-facing driving image taken during daytime, with ample daylight.
Nighttime: A forward-facing driving image taken at night, with dim light and illumination from streetlights or vehicle headlights.
Normal visibility: Good visibility with a clear, open view, allowing distant roads and objects to be seen clearly.
Visibility below 200 m: Poor visibility with blurred distant objects.
Visibility below 100 m: Very poor visibility with a heavily blurred view and indistinct objects ahead.
Visibility below 50 m: Extremely poor visibility with a completely obscured view and no visible road ahead.
